title: Indian-Origin Couple's $20 Million Gift Creates AI College at Texas University
excerpt: Anuradha and Vikas Sinha's donation to the University of North Texas will establish a new College of Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Analytics backed by six permanent endowments.
body:
• Anuradha and Vikas Sinha have donated $20 million to the University of North Texas to establish the Anuradha and Vikas Sinha College of Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Analytics.
  • The gift creates six permanent endowments supporting college leadership, student scholarships, endowed professorships, entrepreneurship and incubation, advanced research, and emerging technologies.
  • The new college will unite work in AI, cybersecurity, data science, advanced analytics, health informatics and learning technologies under two academic divisions and a new Applied Artificial Intelligence and Data Science Institute.
  • The donation follows the couple's 2024 gift establishing UNT's Department of Data Science and a 2025 gift creating the Sinha Innovation Lab for Data Science.

DENTON, Texas — An Indian-origin couple has donated $20 million to the University of North Texas to establish a new college devoted to artificial intelligence and advanced analytics, a gift the university says will reshape how it prepares students for an economy increasingly driven by AI.

The university announced Tuesday that the gift from Anuradha and Vikas Sinha will create the Anuradha and Vikas Sinha College of Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Analytics. The college will serve as an academic and research hub focused on AI, intelligent systems and data analytics, drawing together programmes that now sit across different parts of the university.

Context & Background

Vikas Sinha's path to the donation runs through India and several American universities. He studied at Sri Venkateswara University and in civil engineering at the G. Pulla Reddy Engineering College in Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh, before he and Anuradha moved to the United States for advanced education. Both earned graduate degrees from Florida Atlantic University; Vikas later continued his education at Northwestern University and earned his PhD from the University of North Texas in 2023.

He now serves as vice president of the Mainframe Software Division at Broadcom and has served on the UNT College of Information Leadership Board since 2023, according to the university's announcement.

The $20 million gift extends a growing relationship with UNT. In 2024, the Sinhas gave a gift establishing the Anuradha and Vikas Sinha Department of Data Science, along with endowments supporting scholarships, faculty, research and special initiatives. A year later, they made another major gift creating the Sinha Innovation Lab for Data Science.

Impact & Analysis

The new college will be organized around two academic divisions: the Division of Applied Intelligence and Informatics, focused on building and deploying intelligent systems, and the Division of Information and Learning Applications, focused on how information and intelligent systems operate within human and institutional contexts. It will also house the Applied Artificial Intelligence and Data Science Institute, which the university says will connect AI and analytics research across campus and create opportunities for interdisciplinary research, shared infrastructure, external research funding and industry partnerships.

"What excites us about UNT's vision is that it will go beyond teaching students how to use AI. It will prepare them to build it, understand it, question it, govern it and apply it responsibly — developing both the builders and the stewards of intelligent systems."

— Vikas Sinha

UNT President Harrison Keller said the college advances the university's "Look North: UNT 2030" strategic plan — reshaping how the university prepares students for a changing labour market, accelerating interdisciplinary research and creating economic value for North Texas. The University of North Texas is a public research university and the largest in the Dallas-Fort Worth region, serving nearly 44,000 students across its Denton and Frisco campuses with 230 degree programmes. It awarded more than 13,000 degrees last year.

Diaspora Angle

The Sinhas have framed the gift explicitly in terms of the immigrant experience. "Education has opened doors for us throughout our lives, and we want to hold those doors open for others," Vikas Sinha said in the university's announcement, adding that he and Anuradha believe in what UNT can make possible for students "including those who may come here from another country carrying the same ambition and belief in education that we once did."

"For us, this gift is about paying that opportunity forward and recognising that immigrants don't simply participate in the American dream — they help build it."

— Vikas Sinha

Large philanthropic gifts by Indian-origin donors to American universities have become a visible pattern in recent years, reflecting how wealth created in the US technology sector flows back into public education and research.

What's Next

UNT will celebrate the naming of the college with a university event later this year, the university said. The six endowments — covering college leadership, student scholarships, endowed professorships, entrepreneurship and incubation, advanced research and emerging technologies — are intended to give the college permanent funding as it hires faculty and builds programmes under its two new divisions.
nri_angle: An Indian-American couple's $20 million gift to the University of North Texas shows how immigrant success stories are increasingly shaping American higher education philanthropy.
